messages:
Polestar Ops: Hi team — our latest invoice shows a negative commit credit for our dedicated pool after a large burst yesterday. dashboard shows 1200 reserved hours used, invoice subtracts 1500 credits so balance went negative. Screenshot: https://files.polestar.example/neg-commit.png
Aisha (Support): Sorry for the trouble — can you paste your account id and pool id? also roughly when the burst happened?
Polestar Ops: acct_98765, pool-nyc-3. Burst window: 2029-12-03 22:10 -> 22:48 UTC. Peak concurrency ~3200 rps to that pool.
Aisha (Support): Thanks. @Marta / @Ravi tagging SRE + Billing for telemetry + invoice check. Will start looking at metering logs now.
Marta (SRE): I pulled the metering raw stream for pool-nyc-3. I see a second stream of meter events from our burst-router node between 22:11-22:15 that were duplicated to both "reserved_pool_usage" and "burst_pool_usage". Seems like a dispatcher retry wrote two events for same request id.
Marta (SRE): snippet of what I see:
```
{ request_id: "req-0a1b2c", pool: "pool-nyc-3", type: "reserved", gpu_secs: 0.35 }
{ request_id: "req-0a1b2c", pool: "pool-nyc-3", type: "burst",    gpu_secs: 0.35 }
```
Aisha (Support): That explains double-counted hours — but why did invoice subtract commit credits beyond reserved allocation?
Ravi (Billing): Our billing pipeline dedup step uses (request_id, timestamp_bucket). If a duplicate had slightly shifted timestamp due to clock skew on router host, dedupe missed it and we billed both events. The commit-credit calculation subtracts committed hours first then applies burst hours — double events effectively double-billed.
Ravi (Billing): We see ~2800 extra gpu-seconds attributed across that window (~0.78 reserved GPU-hours). That maps to the negative credit on the invoice.
Polestar Ops: Can you confirm we won't be charged for the duplicate portion? Need to know when this will be corrected for accounting.
Ravi (Billing): Plan: (1) we will flag the duplicated events and roll them back in next invoice cycle and issue a credit for the overlapping gpu-seconds; (2) add a hotfix to the dedupe logic to consider router-host + request_id and a 2s slack window; (3) provide a provisional billing adjustment by EOD UTC.
Marta (SRE): Root cause: router process reconnected mid-request and emitted a second meter event without preserving original request_id timestamp. I'll open an infra PR to make meter emission idempotent and include a monotonic counter. Also adding an alert rule to infra-bot: "meter-dup-detection" when same request_id seen in >1 stream in 60s.
infra-bot: ALERT: pool-nyc-3 meter-dup-detection triggered 2029-12-03T22:16:04Z (count=112)
Aisha (Support): Next steps for Polestar: I'll track the billing credit with @Ravi and confirm once processed. @Polestar Ops — we'll also share a short postmortem and the mitigations. Sorry again, and thanks for the quick report :pray: 
Polestar Ops: Appreciate the quick turnaround. Please include the provisional credit amount so our finance team can reconcile.
Ravi (Billing): Provisional credit: 0.78 GPU-hours (~$64.40 per your reserved rate). We'll apply this as a negative line on next invoice and also issue a one-off refund if you need it sooner — tell us.
Polestar Ops: Please apply refund to expedite. Thanks.
Aisha (Support): Noted. I'll coordinate refund and PM you a timeline. Closing loop when done.
